instructions: Open book. Answer each item from the saved AWS pages and the fact canon only. Give citations for every label: why the key is right and why each other option is wrong. A citation is a fact id or {source_id, quote} with a verbatim quote. Set flag when a second answer is defensible, else null.

items.stem: A company runs a reporting service on Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet. Amazon Linux instances in another subnet of the same VPC call the service on TCP 8443, and every call times out. The client subnet uses the default network ACL. The security group of the service allows inbound TCP 8443 from the security group of the clients. A VPC flow log for the service shows an ACCEPT record for each request and a REJECT record for each response. The company must restore the calls. Which change will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?

options.label: A
options.text: Replace the outbound rules of the network ACL of the service subnet with one rule that allows all traffic to every destination.

options.label: B
options.text: Add an inbound rule to the network ACL of the client subnet that allows TCP ports 32768-61000 from the CIDR block of the service subnet.

options.label: C
options.text: Add an outbound rule to the security group of the service instances that allows TCP ports 32768-61000 to the security group of the clients.

options.label: D
options.text: Add an outbound rule to the network ACL of the service subnet that allows TCP ports 32768-61000 to the CIDR block of the client subnet.
